hero.eyebrow: For lecturers and their students · English & français
hero.body: Clasync is for lecturers who teach several classes, sometimes at more than one school. Check-ins go on the projector, tests and assignments go to students' phones, and the CA adds itself up. Your own AI assistant can do the drafting.
hero.aiLink: New: connect your own AI assistant

attendance.label: Attendance
attendance.before: A sheet passed round the room, then a headcount to catch names written in for friends who stayed home.
attendance.after: A code on the projector that changes every minute, and a count you can check against the room.

assignments.label: Assignments
assignments.before: Work given out loud and forgotten by the next class.
assignments.after: Each assignment is written down and emailed to every student. Anyone who hasn't handed it in gets a reminder the day before.

marks.label: Marks
marks.before: One Excel file per class, kept up to date by hand.
marks.after: The CA works itself out from attendance, assignments, tests and participation. Excel is only for the export.

structure.title: One join. Every course.
structure.body: Clasync follows the way you already teach. You teach at one or more schools, each school has classes, and each class takes your courses. A student joins their class once, with its code and their matricule, and from then on sees every course of that class, from every lecturer, in one place.

schools.title: Several schools, one account
schools.body: Every class you teach is on one dashboard, grouped by school.

shared.title: One class list, shared
shared.body: Colleagues who teach the same class share its student list. They never see your attendance or your marks.

languages.title: English and French
languages.body: Everyone picks their language, and the emails they get follow it.

devices.title: Phones and projectors
devices.body: Nothing to install. Students use their own phones, even on weak data; your screens are made to be read from the back of the room.

attendance.title: A code that changes every minute
attendance.body: You put the code on the projector and students type it on their phones. It changes every 60 seconds, so checking in for a friend who isn't there is a lot harder than writing their name on a sheet.

points.twoCheckIns: Two check-ins, at the start and the end of class. Students who do both are marked present.
points.liveCount: You open and close each check-in, and watch the count go up live.
points.campus: If you turn it on, students have to be near the school to check in.
points.corrections: A grid per course shows every session. You can change any mark by hand, and Clasync notes who changed it.

example.label: Example: attendance history for a course

assignments.title: Work nobody forgets
assignments.body: Give the work in writing, once, and let Clasync do the chasing.

points.drafts: Write it as a draft. Publishing it emails every student.
points.formats: Students type an answer, upload files, or both. A photo of a handwritten page works too.
points.reminder: The day before it's due, a reminder goes to the students who haven't handed anything in.
points.late: You decide whether late work is accepted. If it is, you see how late each one was.
points.release: Mark one submission at a time, then release all the grades together. Each student sees only their own.

tests.title: Tests in class, on their phones
tests.body: Set the test once and share its link. It opens only when you press Start in class, and multiple choice marks itself.

points.start: Schedule it ahead. Nobody sees a question until you start it in the room.
points.types: Multiple choice, marked automatically, and short answers.
points.timer: The timer runs on the server. A refresh or a dropped connection loses nothing, and answers sync when the connection comes back.
points.leaving: Leaving the test for another tab or app is detected and logged. You choose how many exits are allowed, and you can let a student back in.
points.results: Releasing results emails each student. Multiple choice shows as one total, so the right answers stay private.

ca.title: The CA adds itself up
ca.body: Decide once how the CA is made up. Every student's mark stays current as attendance, assignments, tests and participation come in.

points.split: Out of 30 by default, and you can change it. Split it across attendance, assignments, tests and participation.
points.weights: Give any item more weight, and count the best N of M tests.
points.participation: Tap +1 or −1 beside a name during class for participation.
points.views: Students see their own breakdown. You see the whole class, and who is slipping.
points.export: Export to Excel: matricule, name, each component and the CA total.

notes.title: Every course's material, in one place
notes.body: No more PDFs lost in the WhatsApp group. Each course keeps its notes, files and links by topic, with practice questions for revision, and students can search all of it from their phone.

points.resources: Topics in your order. Each holds notes written in the editor, files (PDF, Word, PowerPoint) and links.
points.share: Share a note with your other courses. Edit it once and it changes everywhere.
points.practice: Practice questions are untimed, give instant feedback, and never count toward the CA.
points.fromTest: One click turns a finished test's questions into revision. Students see them once the results are out.

assistant.title: Your own AI assistant, connected to your classes
assistant.body: Clasync works with the assistant you already use. Connect Claude, ChatGPT or another MCP tool, then ask about your classes or have it draft the work. It acts as you, with exactly your permissions, and everything it writes stays a draft until you publish it.

marking.title: Short answers, marked faster
marking.body: When you mark a test, every short answer comes with a suggested mark and a one-line reason, drawn from your own marking guide. You confirm it or pick another mark. Nothing is final until you do, and there is no “accept all”.

points.byQuestion: Mark one question at a time, across the whole class.
points.hidden: Names are hidden while you mark, unless you show them.
points.private: Students never see a suggestion, only the mark you confirm.

private.q: Who can see my students' marks?
private.a: Only you. Colleagues who teach the same class share its student list and nothing else, and each student sees only their own marks.

drafts.q: Can the AI send anything to my students?
drafts.a: No. Whatever your assistant writes and every suggested mark is a draft, and it never emails a student. Only you publish, start a test or release results.

access.a: What you can see in Clasync, and nothing more. It signs in as you, with your permissions, so it never reaches another lecturer's courses.

data.q: Where do students' answers go when a mark is suggested?
data.a: To suggest a mark, Clasync sends that answer and your marking guide to an AI model. It happens only when you open that question for marking.

cheating.q: Does Clasync stop cheating in tests?
cheating.a: No browser can lock a phone. Clasync detects and records every time a student leaves the test, ends it after the number of exits you allow, and leaves the decision to you.

connection.q: What if a student's connection drops mid-test?
connection.a: Their answers stay on the phone and sync when the connection returns. The timer runs on the server, so a refresh doesn't reset it, and a lost connection never counts as leaving.

install.q: Do students need to install an app?
install.a: No. Clasync runs in the phone's browser, and photos are shrunk before they upload to save data.

practice.q: Does revision practice count toward the CA?
practice.a: Never. Practice is private to each student, and you don't see who practised or how they did.

collect.title: What Clasync keeps
collect.account: Your account: name, email address, whether you are a lecturer or a student, and your language.
collect.google: If you use Continue with Google: the name and email address of your Google account. Clasync never sees your Google password.
collect.classes: Your classes and courses: your matricule, attendance, assignments and the files you hand in, test answers, marks and continuous assessment (CA).
collect.tests: During a test: when you leave the test page and for how long, so your lecturer can see it.
collect.location: At an attendance check-in only: your position at that moment, to confirm you are at the school. Clasync does not follow your location at any other time.
collect.signIns: When you sign in: the IP address and browser of that session, to keep your account secure.

access.title: Who can see it
access.lecturers: Your lecturers see your work, marks and attendance for the courses they teach, and nothing from other lecturers' courses.
access.you: You see your own classes, work and marks.
access.admins: The Clasync administrator sees counts and account details (name, email, role) to keep the service running. The admin pages never show marks, test answers, submitted work or anyone's attendance.
access.sold: Clasync does not sell your data, show ads or track you across other sites.

services.title: Services Clasync relies on
services.intro: Clasync uses a few providers to run. Each one only gets what it needs for its job:
services.vercel: Vercel hosts the app and stores uploaded files.
services.email: Resend sends emails such as verification links and assignment reminders.
services.errors: Sentry receives error reports so problems can be fixed, with IP addresses removed.
services.push: If you turn on notifications, the push service of your browser's maker (Google, Apple, Mozilla or Microsoft) delivers them to your device. It only sees an encrypted message.
services.ai: Vercel AI Gateway sends a written test answer and its question to an AI model when a lecturer asks for a suggested mark, without your name, matricule or email. The lecturer decides the mark.
services.google: Google, only if you choose Continue with Google.

assistants.title: AI assistants connected by lecturers
assistants.body: A lecturer can connect an AI assistant (such as Claude or ChatGPT) to their own Clasync account. The assistant can read that lecturer's courses, including students' work and marks, to help them, and can only create drafts that the lecturer reviews. It cannot publish anything, send emails or see other lecturers' courses. What the assistant reads is also handled by its provider, under that provider's privacy policy.

cookies.title: Cookies
cookies.body: Clasync only uses cookies to keep you signed in and to remember your language. There are no advertising or analytics cookies.

rights.title: Your choices
rights.edit: You can change your name and language in Settings, and add your matricule to a class.
rights.google: You can connect or disconnect Google in Settings.
rights.delete: To get a copy of your data or have your account deleted, write to <email>{address}</email>. Deleting an account deletes its data with it.
rights.keep: Clasync keeps your data while your account exists.

changes.title: Changes to this page
changes.body: If this policy changes, the date at the top of the page changes too. Important changes will be announced in the app.

footer.tagline: Attendance, assignments, tests and marks for lecturers who teach across several classes and schools.

terms.title: Terms of use
terms.description: The rules for using Clasync, for lecturers and students.
terms.intro: These terms apply to everyone who uses Clasync at clasync.online. By creating an account, you accept them. They go with the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>, which explains what Clasync keeps about you. For any question, write to <email>{address}</email>.

accounts.title: Your account
accounts.real: Use your real name and an email address you can read. Students should enter their matricule as their school gives it.
accounts.yours: An account is for one person. Keep your password to yourself, and write to <email>{address}</email> if you think someone else has used your account.
accounts.lecturers: Lecturers are responsible for the classes and courses they create, and for having their school's agreement to run them in Clasync.

use.title: Fair use
use.checkIn: Don't check in for someone who isn't in the room, or pass check-in codes to people outside it.
use.others: Don't try to see or change other people's classes, marks or work.
use.tests: Don't get help from someone else during a test, or use their account, unless your lecturer allows it.
use.content: Don't upload anything illegal or harmful, or anything you don't have the right to share.
use.service: Don't disrupt the service, probe it for weaknesses, or collect data from it automatically.

content.title: Your work and materials
content.own: What you upload stays yours: notes, assignments, answers and files.
content.license: You allow Clasync to store it and show it to the people it is meant for, such as your lecturer or the students of your course, only to run the service.
content.marks: Lecturers set marks, attendance and CA. If you think one is wrong, talk to your lecturer.

ai.title: AI features
ai.suggestions: Suggested marks come from an AI model and can be wrong. Nothing counts until the lecturer confirms it.
ai.assistants: An AI assistant connected by a lecturer works with that lecturer's access and only creates drafts. The lecturer stays responsible for what they publish.

service.title: The service
service.body: Clasync is provided as it is. It is looked after carefully, but it may sometimes be interrupted or contain mistakes, and features may change as it improves. Keep your own copy of anything you can't afford to lose, such as the CA export.

ending.title: Suspension and leaving
ending.leave: You can stop using Clasync at any time. To have your account deleted, follow the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.
ending.suspend: Clasync may suspend an account that breaks these terms or puts other users at risk. A suspended user can write to <email>{address}</email> to ask why.

liability.title: Responsibility
liability.body: As far as the law allows, Clasync is not responsible for indirect losses, or for decisions based on marks, attendance or AI suggestions that were not checked.

changes.title: Changes to these terms
changes.body: If these terms change, the date at the top of the page changes too. Important changes will be announced in the app before they apply.

about.title: Built for lecturers who teach in more than one place.
about.description: Why Clasync exists and what it holds to.

story.title: Why Clasync
story.p1: Many lecturers teach the same course to several classes, often at more than one school. Each class comes with its own attendance sheets, its own Excel file of marks and its own group chat for assignments.
story.p2: Clasync brings all of it into one place. Check-ins go on the projector, work and tests are handed in from a phone, and the CA works itself out. The time saved goes back to teaching.

lecturers.title: Lecturers stay in charge
lecturers.body: AI suggests and drafts. Nothing reaches students until a lecturer approves it.

privacy.title: Students' data stays private
privacy.body: No ads, no selling, no tracking. Each person sees only what concerns them.

phone.title: Made for the phone in every pocket
phone.body: Nothing to install, English and French, and photos shrunk before upload to save data.

contact.title: Get in touch
contact.body: Questions, ideas, or a school that wants to use Clasync: we'd like to hear from you.

changelog.title: What's new
changelog.description: Everything that has shipped in Clasync, newest first.

app.title: Install Clasync as an app
app.body: Add Clasync to your phone or computer and open it like any other app.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.body: Get a notification for attendance check-in, tests, new notes, assignments and results. Turn them on or off in Settings.

google.title: Sign in with Google
google.body: Create an account or sign in with your Google account, and connect or disconnect Google from Settings.

legal.title: Privacy policy, terms and security pages
legal.body: Plain-words pages, in English and French, on what Clasync keeps, the rules of use and how your data is protected.

matricule.title: Join before you have a matricule
matricule.body: Students can join a class right away and add their matricule later.

receipts.title: Email receipts
receipts.body: Students get an email for every assignment and test they hand in, and class joins are confirmed to everyone concerned.

links.title: One-tap links
links.body: Share a link that joins a class in one tap, or a check-in link while attendance is open.

checklist.title: Setup checklist
checklist.body: New lecturers and students see the few steps to get going on their dashboard, ticked off as they go.

assistant.title: Connect your AI assistant
assistant.body: Claude, ChatGPT or any MCP app can read your courses and draft assignments, tests, notes and marks. Nothing reaches students until you approve it.

notes.title: Notes and revision
notes.body: Share notes, files and links with a course, and give students practice rounds before a test.

tests.title: Tests on students' phones
tests.body: Write a test, run it in class, mark short answers question by question with AI suggestions, and release the results.

ca.title: Continuous assessment
ca.body: The CA works itself out from attendance, assignments, tests and participation, with an Excel export.

launch.title: First version
launch.body: Schools, shared classes with join codes, courses, attendance with a rotating code on the projector, and assignments with reminders, in English and French.

forSchools.title: Bring your whole department.
forSchools.description: Clasync for departments and schools: attendance, assignments, tests and CA for every lecturer, in one place.
forSchools.lead: When every lecturer in a department uses Clasync, attendance is checked the same way, the CA follows the same rules, and students find all their courses in one place.

attendance.title: Attendance you can trust
attendance.body: A code on the projector that changes every minute, and a check that the student is at the school.

ca.title: The same CA everywhere
ca.body: The CA works itself out from attendance, assignments, tests and participation, and exports to Excel.

shared.title: Classes shared between lecturers
shared.body: Colleagues who teach the same class share its student list, and nothing else.

phone.title: Nothing to install
phone.body: It runs in the phone's browser, in English and French, and saves students' data.

talk.title: Write to us
talk.body: Tell us about your school and departments, and we'll help your lecturers get started.

setup.title: Lecturers set up their classes
setup.body: Each lecturer creates an account, finds the school and adds their classes and courses in a few minutes.

join.title: Students join with a code
join.body: Students join from their phone with the class code or a one-tap link.

contact.title: Talk to us
contact.body: Questions about a department or a whole school? Write to us.
contact.subject: Clasync for our school

security.title: Security
security.description: How Clasync protects lecturers' and students' data.
security.intro: Clasync holds students' work and marks, so it is built to keep them to the people who should see them. This page explains how. What Clasync keeps, and why, is in the <privacy>privacy policy</privacy>.

accounts.title: Accounts and sign-in
accounts.passwords: Passwords are stored hashed, never in plain text. You can also sign in with Google instead.
accounts.verify: An email address must be confirmed before the account is used.
accounts.limits: Sign-in and sign-up attempts are rate-limited to slow down password guessing.
accounts.suspend: A suspended account is refused everywhere: at sign-in, on every page and through AI assistants.

access.title: Who can see what
access.lecturers: Each lecturer sees only their own courses. Colleagues who share a class share its student list, and nothing else.
access.students: Students see only their own work, marks and attendance.
access.admins: The admin pages never show marks, test answers, submitted work or attendance. Every admin action is recorded in an audit log.

data.title: Data and files
data.files: Uploaded files are kept in private storage and only shown to people allowed to see them.
data.errors: Error reports have IP addresses removed.
data.sold: No ads, no selling of data, no tracking across other sites.

ai.title: AI
ai.suggest: AI only suggests. A mark counts only once the lecturer confirms it.
ai.names: When a mark is suggested, the AI service sees the question, the marking guide and the answer, never a name, matricule or email.
ai.assistants: A connected AI assistant works with its lecturer's access, can only create drafts and is rate-limited. Lecturers see connected assistants in Settings and can disconnect them at any time.

integrity.title: Fair attendance and tests
integrity.codes: Check-in codes change every minute, and a check-in also confirms the student is at the school.
integrity.timer: A test's timer runs on the server, so refreshing the page doesn't reset it.
integrity.leave: Leaving the test page is recorded and shown to the lecturer.

report.title: Reporting a problem
report.body: If you find a security problem, write to <email>{address}</email>. Please don't share it publicly until it is fixed.
